title: Observed Regional Fluxes to Constrain Modeled Estimates of the Ocean Carbon Sink
testbed_rationale: The study does not provide training/evaluation datasets for subgrid-scale physical parameterizations; it performs a diagnostic evaluation and emergent constraint style filtering of GCM hindcast models using existing gridded pCO2 products.
pain_points: Severe regional divergence among ocean biogeochemical models despite agreement on the globally integrated carbon sink (regional compensation of errors).
Large uncertainty in natural carbon outgassing driven by riverine carbon loads (0.49 ± 0.53 PgC/yr), which dominates observational uncertainty in multiple ocean regions.
Sparse spatial and temporal sampling of in-situ surface pCO2 observations (SOCAT covers only 1.5% of 1° × 1° monthly grid boxes), limiting skill in reconstructing interannual variability.
Systematic underestimation of net primary production and carbon uptake by hindcast models in subtropical gyres despite reproducing seasonal timing.
extraction_notes: The machine learning methods catalogued are those underlying the diagnostic observation-based pCO2 products evaluated in the study (MPI-SOMFFN, CMEMS-FFNN, NIES-FNN, LDEO-HPD, CSIR-ML6). The authors themselves do not train new ML models in this paper.
